chunks: One of our companions, from Ibn Jamhour, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yusuf ibn al-Sukht al-Basri, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi al-Bilad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mihran, all from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said:

We were in Medina, and Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it. So I said, 'Shaving it is preferable,' and Zurara said, 'Plucking it is preferable.' So we sought permission to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he permitted us while he was in the bathhouse waxing; he had already waxed his armpits. So I said to Zurara, 'Do you suffice with that?' He said, 'No, perhaps he did this for what is not permissible for me to do.'

He said, 'In what are you?' So I said, 'Zurara disputed with me regarding plucking the armpit and shaving it; I said shaving is preferable, and he said plucking is preferable.' He said, 'You have hit the Sunnah and Zurara erred. Shaving it is preferable to plucking it, and waxing it is preferable to shaving it.' Then he said to us, 'Go and get waxed.' We said, 'We did that three days ago.' He said, 'Repeat it, for waxing is a cleanser.'
ai.seo_question: What is the preferred method for removing armpit hair according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the scholarly debate between Zarrara and the narrator regarding armpit hair removal, establishing a clear hierarchy: waxing (al-itala') is superior to shaving, which in turn is superior to plucking. The Imam further clarifies that while the methods differ in merit, the act of waxing itself is considered a form of ritual purity (tahur), reinforcing the Shia emphasis on both physical cleanliness and spiritual purification in daily practices.
